details.description: This is Google Cloud Speech-to-Text's V1 API transcription service in its default configuration, with Google's opt-in data logging program not enabled. By default, Cloud Speech-to-Text does not log customer audio data or transcripts, per Google's Data Logging documentation; a project only has its audio and transcripts logged if it explicitly opts into the data logging program, which this configuration has not done. Data sent to a project without data logging enabled is used by Google only as needed to provide the service, not to refine or improve its products, per Google's Data Logging documentation.
advantages: Audio and transcripts are not logged by Google, since data logging is off by default on Cloud Speech-to-Text, per Google's Data Logging documentation.
Speech-to-Text API includes recognition features such as automatic punctuation and word-level confidence, per Google's Speech-to-Text documentation.
disadvantages: Does not receive the discounted pricing that Google offers to projects that opt into the data logging program, per Google's Data Logging documentation.
use_cases: Transcribing spoken audio to text via the Speech-to-Text V1 API for customers who do not want their audio or transcripts logged by Google, per Google's Data Logging documentation.

notes: Google's Data Logging documentation (part of the Cloud Speech-to-Text V1 docs) describes data logging as a project-level opt-in, not a named recognition model, and does not say which specific V1 model(s) (Standard, Enhanced, Chirp, etc.) it applies to, so this entry describes the default (non-logging) configuration of the service rather than a distinct recognition architecture. No pricing figures, WER numbers or exact language list were stated on the pages opened, so evaluations and languages are left empty. Google's release notes show no deprecation of the V1 API.
